summary:
# NOTES: *Copper Coleson's Ghost* by Edward P. Hendrick (1930, L. C. Page & Co.; illus. Harold Cue). Dedicated to Bob and Jack. Single book, no BOOK headings.

## Setting / people
- Town of **Truesdell** (Lake Erie shore). Blake homestead: white cottage, great apple tree (planted ~70 yrs ago from half-eaten apple core of **Josiah Blake**, "six feet two," great-grandfather of Ned). Grindstone under tree.
- **Ned Blake** (17, ~<70 in., <150 lb, gray eyes, athletic, captain, pitcher, trumpet; leader; carries camp axe).
- **Tommy "Fatty" Beals** (plump, wheezy; treasurer; soap box; catcher; family servant **Sam**, Samuel G. Washington, a negro cook/servant).
- **Dave "Weary" Wilbur** (lanky, lazy drawl, straw in mouth, proverbs, owns flivver (battered car), southpaw pitcher, clarinet; garage used for meetings).
- **Dick Somers** (new boy, freckled, wide mouth, blue eyes; family moved in next door; banjo; center field; fast). Mother Mrs. Somers.
- **Charlie "Red" Rogers** (red hair, peppery, saxophone, fielder; sprained ankle in game 1; Tapley/Wat).
- **Jim Tapley** (piano, orchestra leader). **Wat Sanford** (drums/traps, superstitious). **Abner "Bony" Jones** (sallow, knocker; job at Pavilion dance hall). **Tinker Owen** (flunked math).
- **Dan "Slugger" Slade** (big bully from Bedford; third base; later works for Latrobe in Canada).
- **Eli "Copper" Coleson** (old copper miner; long white beard green-stained; built unfinished brick mansion "Coleson's Folly" on Lake Erie shore ~10 mi out; mine collapsed; presumed dead).
- **Latrobe** (ex-partner, claims share; ugly; diver; swarthy face; bootlegger leader).
- **Miller** (tall, red-faced). **Casey** (burly, club). Short thick-set man in fur coat = Latrobe.
- **Inspector Baker** (Cleveland police).
- Truck: small auto-truck with canvas top. Tug/steamer **Irma**. Red Canadian Club whisky.

## Events (in order)
1. Ch I: Ned grinds axe; Dave turns crank, Tommy sits; new neighbor Dick Somers unloading furniture. Slade bullies Dick, bends square iron poker into U; Ned straightens it (shifting grip, extended thumbs), then bends/straightens cleanly. Ice cream soda treat (Tommy's).
2. Ch II: Swim at Coleson's; Ned explains mine history (Eli found copper digging well; ripped farmhouse with dynamite; vein petered out; partly finished mansion; shaft ~15 ft deep; windlass). Red Rogers joins.
3. Ch III: Coleson's mine caved; Latrobe reported he could not find him; dredge recovers ore; Latrobe dives; Coleson presumed dead; house shuttered; ghost rumors (dancing lights, dark man).
4. Ch IV: Winter; ice-boat *Frost King* (Ned's). Mysterious fur-coated passenger pays $15 + $10 (Canadian bills) to race Detroit express to Cleveland. Crack in ice jumped (~6 ft). Beat express by 5 min. Ch V: Ned overhears same man (Latrobe, unnamed) on phone at Cleveland hotel with Miller; "Local nothing!"; blizzard ends ice-boating; $15 divided.
5. Ch VI–VII: Baseball. Rogers hurt ankle; Tinker Owen flunked math. Big game vs Bedford: Slade's belt-hook interference on Dick at third base; Ned tricks Slade with belt at 3rd (run awarded); Ned's fingers torn (pitching hand) in 8th; Dave pitches; Slade hits liner, Dick leaps, Ned catches for final out. Win 3–2.
6. Ch VIII–IX: Summer plan — dances at Coleson house. Seven members: Ned, Tommy (treasurer, refreshments), Dave, Wat (drums/decor), Dick, Rogers, Tapley. Lease for $25/month, 90 days, put in Sam's name ($75 total later; expires end Sept). Cleaning, scraping floors (wax, brooms $4 etc.), covering cellar opening with floor.
7. Ch X: Posters "DEMON DANCES at the HAUNTED COLESON HOUSE... Grand Opening Sat. July 7; Music by the Syncopating Six; Admission $1.00 a Couple." Letter to Sam signed "Eli Coleson": "...you black son of Satan! ... I'll haunt you to your dying day."
8. Ch XI: Sam scared. Opening dance: candles extinguished by gust; spot of light crawls along wall; first dance $86 admissions + $17.50 refreshments.
9. Ch XII: Ned pays lease Monday ($75). Sam: saw "Eli Coleson" face with white beard at window Saturday night; rubber-soled footprint under window. Boys scout via Cedar Hollow; new white paint on range stake and chimney mark; note on front door: "I don't want company here. E. C."
10. Ch XIII–XIV: Night watch: Rogers & Tommy; saw grayish mist and hunched figure in lightning; Ned & Dick see tug lights, searchlight tracing ranges, marking buoy rising from lake; fresh oil spot in old wood-road.
11. Ch XV: Wood-road (grown-over, vine curtain on oak). Abandoned wood-cutters' shanty; ants carrying bread crumbs; fire-warden poster torn corner matches Coleson note fragment. Tire tracks vanish at end of road.
12. Ch XVI–XVII: Ned's list of facts. Night stakeout with Dave; shanty light, man inside; truck arrives; talk about "Irma" (tug name); slabs knocked down; Ned recognizes Latrobe (diver) as fur-coat man.
13. Ch XVIII: Dave sick; Saturday dance #2 (95 admissions). Apparition: long-bearded man with pickax; boys chase; man vanishes; Ned finds rubber-soled print. Ned reveals Latrobe.
14. Ch XIX: Stakeout behind house; capture of Slugger Slade by Ned (diving tackle), Tommy's weight. Slade reveals hidden pivot foundation slab (swings on pins; white stone trigger).
15. Ch XX–XXI: Cellar; false wig/beard and painted pickax; oak door to mine; bats; dump-car on rails; small cable/buoy winch; Ned and Dick ride car into flooded tunnel; car reaches end underwater; boxes of whisky. Boys locked in by Latrobe/Slade.
16. Ch XXII–XXIII: Boys rehearse Ned's dive plan (seventy-six seconds from car hitting water to stop). Ned swims out with loaded car; boys wait 15+ min; Ned opens door. Hide. Latrobe, Miller, Slade, Casey arrive; canvas walkway on ground; they blast/escape; Latrobe orders them left to starve.
17. Ch XXIV: Ned phones Cleveland from Cedar Hollow gas station; Inspector Baker; chase in wood-road; Slade throws case of whisky in road; truck crashes shanty; gasoline explosion; Latrobe, Miller, Slade arrested (Slade escapes, per Dick "at rate ... Rocky Mountains"; Latrobe, Miller, Casey caught).
18. Ch XXV: Profits: Monday meeting in Blake apple tree; plan: sell dance tickets with mine tours; clear wood-road; Ned asks Dave to grind axe. "THE END."

## Key quotes
- Dave: "Use your bean!"; "A barking dog seldom bites."
- Ned on bending: "Bending a bar is much like mischief. It's easier to do than to undo."
- Slade: "I'll bend you like I bend this here poker!"
- Dick: "Zowie!"; Tommy: "Gosh!"; Red: "Horsefeathers!"
